questions.stem: Chromatography can be used to separate the substances in a mixture.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Diagram 1 shows the apparatus used to separate the different dyes in a food colouring. The box lists some terms used in chromatography. Use the terms from the box to label diagram 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Diagram 2 shows a chromatogram produced using four different food colourings, P, Q, R and S. $\begin{array}{c c c c c} \hline \mathrm {P} & \mathrm {Q} & \mathrm {R} & \mathrm {S} \\ \hline \end{array}$ finish Diagram 2

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Which food colouring contains only one dye? A P B Q C R D S

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Which food colourings have one dye in common? A P, Q and R B P, R and S C Q, R and S D P, Q, R and S

parts.label: b-iii

questions.stem: The diagram shows the apparatus used to prepare carbon dioxide in the laboratory.

parts.label: a
parts.text: What is the name of the piece of apparatus containing the dilute hydrochloric acid? A burette B pipette C tap funnel D thistle funnel

parts.label: b
parts.text: Complete the chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which of these is a true statement about carbon dioxide? A it turns red litmus blue B it turns limewater milky C it relights a glowing spill D it burns with a squeaky pop

parts.label: d-i
parts.text: Give a reason why carbon dioxide can be collected by downward delivery in air.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Give another method of collecting carbon dioxide.

parts.text: When carbon dioxide dissolves in water, a weakly acidic solution forms. Suggest a pH value for this solution.

The equation for this reaction is $\mathrm {C u C O} _ {3} (\mathrm {s}) \rightarrow \mathrm {C u O} (\mathrm {s}) + \mathrm {C O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$ State the change in colour of the solid when copper(II) carbonate decomposes. from

parts.label: g
parts.text: Suggest two properties of carbon dioxide that make it suitable for use in fire extinguishers.

questions.stem: A teacher investigates the reaction between sodium and water. The teacher fills a trough with water. She adds a few drops of litmus solution to the water, and then adds a piece of sodium.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The sodium floats on the water. It reacts with the water and produces bubbles of hydrogen gas.

parts.label: a-i
parts.text: State two other observations that are made during the reaction.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Balance the equation for the reaction between sodium and water. Include the state symbols.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Lithium and potassium react in a similar way to sodium when added to water.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: State why they have a similar reaction in terms of the electronic configurations of their atoms.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Place the elements lithium, potassium and sodium in order of reactivity. most reactive least reactive

questions.stem: Use the Periodic Table on page 2 to help you answer this question.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Which word correctly describes substances found in the Periodic Table? A alloys B compounds C elements D mixtures

parts.label: b
parts.text: The substances in the Periodic Table are arranged in order of increasing A atomic number B mass number C nucleon number D relative atomic mass

parts.label: c
parts.text: The table lists properties of some of the gases in Group 0 of the Periodic Table. Complete the table by giving the symbol for neon an estimate for the boiling point of argon the reaction of xenon with metals

parts.label: d
parts.text: The photograph shows an electric light bulb. The tungsten filament becomes very hot when the light bulb is switched on. Suggest why argon is a more suitable gas than air to use in the light bulb.

questions.stem: A student tries to make a pure, dry sample of hydrated cobalt(II) chloride crystals. He uses dilute hydrochloric acid and solid cobalt(II) oxide. This is the student's method. Step 1 pour about $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of dilute hydrochloric acid into a beaker Step 2 warm the acid using a Bunsen burner Step 3 add a small amount of cobalt(II) oxide and stir the mixture with a glass rod Step 4 add further small amounts of cobalt(II) oxide until it stops reacting Step 5 filter the final mixture and collect the filtrate in an evaporating basin Step 6 leave the filtrate until all of the water has evaporated His sample of cobalt(II) oxide contains a small amount of a solid impurity that dissolves in water, but does not react with the acid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State why it is not necessary to have a precise measurement of the volume of hydrochloric acid in step 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State why the acid is warmed in step 2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why a glass rod, rather than a metal spatula, is used to stir the mixture in step 3. (1)

parts.label: d
parts.text: State how the student will know when the cobalt(II) oxide stops reacting in step 4.

parts.label: e
parts.text: State why the method used in step 6 will not produce a pure sample of hydrated cobalt(II) chloride crystals.

parts.label: f
parts.text: Describe how the student could produce a pure, dry sample of crystals from the filtrate in step 5.

parts.label: g
parts.text: The table shows the formula and colour of three different types of cobalt(II) chloride. When water is added very slowly to solid $ \mathrm{C o C l_{2}} $ , the colour of $ \mathrm{C o C l_{2}} $ changes from blue to purple and then to pink.

parts.label: g-i
parts.text: Write a chemical equation for the change from the purple solid to the pink solid.

parts.label: g-ii
parts.text: Which of these words describes the change taking place when the pink solid is heated to form the blue solid? A crystallisation B dehydration C hydration D redox

questions.stem: Tests are done on a sample of a solid, X. Solid X contains the ammonium ion, $ \mathrm{N H_{4}^{+}} $ , one other cation and one anion. The table lists details of the tests done on solid X and the observations made for each test.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Identify the gas given off in test 1.

parts.label: b

parts.text: State what test 3A and test 3B tell you about solid X. test 3A test 3B

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: Identify the anion in solid X.

questions.stem: Antimony, Sb, is an element in Group 5 of the Periodic Table. The mineral, stibnite, contains antimony sulfide, $ \mathrm{S b_{2} S_{3}} $ Antimony can be obtained from stibnite in a two-stage process. Stage 1 stibnite is roasted in air $\mathrm {S b} _ {2} \mathrm {S} _ {3} + 5 \mathrm {O} _ {2} \rightarrow \mathrm {S b} _ {2} \mathrm {O} _ {4} + 3 \mathrm {S O} _ {2}$ Stage 2 the oxide produced is heated with carbon to form antimony and carbon dioxide (a) (i) State why the sulfur in stage 1 is said to be oxidised. (ii) Complete the equation for the reaction in stage 2. $\mathrm {S b} _ {2} \mathrm {O} _ {4} + \dots \dots \dots \mathrm {C} \rightarrow \dots \dots \dots \mathrm {S b} + \dots \dots \dots \mathrm {C O} _ {2}$

parts.label: b
parts.text: Bismuth is another element in Group 5 of the Periodic Table. Bismuth forms an oxide, $ \mathrm{B i_{2} O_{3}} $ , which has a giant ionic structure.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Give the formula of the bismuth ion in bismuth oxide.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Explain why bismuth oxide has a high melting point.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: Bismuth oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid to form bismuth chloride. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

questions.stem: A student investigates the rate of reaction between zinc and hydrochloric acid, using an excess of zinc powder. She uses this apparatus. The student measures the volume of gas in the syringe every minute for ten minutes. The table shows her results.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Plot the student's results on the grid.

parts.label: a-ii
parts.text: Draw a curve of best fit. Volume of gas in $ cm^{3} $ Time in minutes

parts.label: b
parts.text: The result at two minutes is anomalous.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Suggest a mistake that the student could have made to produce this anomalous result.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Use your graph to estimate the volume of gas that was given off at two minutes. Show clearly on your graph how you obtain your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the last four readings for the volume of gas are the same.

parts.label: d
parts.text: State how the graph shows that the rate of reaction decreases during the first seven minutes.

parts.label: d-ii
parts.text: Explain, in terms of the particle collision theory, why the rate of reaction decreases during the first seven minutes.

questions.stem: This apparatus is used to test whether magnesium, solid magnesium chloride and an aqueous solution of magnesium chloride conduct electricity. The table shows the results. Explain these results, with reference to the type of particles in each substance.
Bromine is a red-brown liquid at room temperature. Liquid bromine forms a brown gas when warmed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain what happens to the bromine molecules when liquid bromine is warmed to form a gas.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Bromine reacts with water to form a mixture of hydrobromic acid, HBr, and hypobromous acid, HBrO. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hydrobromic acid reacts with magnesium carbonate to form a solution containing magnesium bromide. $\mathrm {M g C O} _ {3} (\mathrm {s}) + 2 \mathrm {H B r} (\mathrm {a q}) \rightarrow \mathrm {M g B r} _ {2} (\mathrm {a q}) + \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} (\mathrm {I}) + \mathrm {C O} _ {2} (\mathrm {g})$ Crystals of hydrated magnesium bromide, $ \mathrm{M g B r}_{2}. 6 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} $ , can be obtained from this solution. $\mathrm {M g B r} _ {2} + 6 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O} \rightarrow \mathrm {M g B r} _ {2}. 6 \mathrm {H} _ {2} \mathrm {O}$

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: An excess of hydrobromic acid is reacted with 0.125 mol of magnesium carbonate. Show, by calculation, that the maximum theoretical mass of hydrated magnesium bromide that can be made is 36.5 g. $ [ M_{r} $ of $ \mathrm{M g B r_{2}. 6 H_{2} O}=2 9 2 ] $

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: In an experiment using 0.125 mol of magnesium carbonate, with an excess of hydrobromic acid, the mass of hydrated magnesium bromide obtained is 26.4 g. Suggest two reasons why the actual mass obtained is less than the maximum theoretical mass.

questions.stem: Malachite is an ore of copper containing copper(II) carbonate and several other compounds that are insoluble in water. You are supplied with several pieces of malachite, these chemicals and items of apparatus. Chemicals: dilute sulfuric acid magnesium powder Apparatus: beakers filter funnel and paper pestle and mortar Describe how you would use the chemicals and the apparatus to obtain a sample of copper from the malachite.

parts.text: Which property of hydrocarbons is used to separate crude oil into fractions? A boiling point B chemical reactivity C density D melting point

parts.label: b

parts.label: b-i

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Give one use for kerosene.

parts.label: b-iii
parts.text: State which fraction is the most viscous.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Catalytic cracking is used to break down long-chain alkanes into shorter-chain alkanes and alkenes.

parts.label: c-i
parts.text: Name the catalyst used in industrial cracking.

parts.label: c-ii
parts.text: State the temperature used in industrial cracking.

parts.label: c-iii
parts.text: Tetradecane $ \mathrm{(C_{1 4} H_{3 0})} $ can be cracked to make ethene $ \mathrm{(C_{2} H_{4})} $ and only one other hydrocarbon. Write a chemical equation for this reaction.

parts.label: c-iv

parts.label: c-v
parts.text: Name the polymer formed from ethene.

parts.label: c-vi
parts.text: Explain why this polymer is difficult to dispose of.

Experiment 1 1. 0 mol/dm $ ^{3} $ $ \mathrm{H_{2} S O_{4}} $ temperature after one minute Experiment 3

questions.stem: A teacher uses this apparatus to demonstrate the electrolysis of molten zinc chloride. crystals of a shiny, grey solid form at one of the electrodes a pale green substance forms at the other electrode the lamp goes out after the teacher stops heating the zinc chloride A student records these observations.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by the term electrolysis.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State why graphite is more suitable to use for the electrodes than magnesium in this electrolysis.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Which of these is a correct statement for this electrolysis? A the pale green substance is chloride B both products are elements C the pale green substance forms at the negative electrode D the shiny grey solid is zinc chloride

parts.label: d
parts.text: The student writes this ionic half-equation for the reaction that forms the pale green substance. $2 \mathrm {C l} ^ {-} + 2 \mathrm {e} ^ {-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm {C l}$ Identify the two mistakes in her ionic half-equation.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The lamp goes out after the teacher stops heating the zinc chloride, because electrons are no longer flowing through the wires. Explain why electrons are no longer flowing through the wires.
